questions.question: In which year did Abhinav Bindra create history by becoming the first Indian to win an individual gold medal at the Olympic Games in the 10-meter Air Rifle event?

The correct answer is __**2008**__.

questions.question:
Read the following about Revenue Receipts.

A. Revenue receipts are those receipts that do not lead to a claim on the government.

B. Revenue receipts are divided into tax and non-tax revenues.

Identify the CORRECT statement/statements.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and B**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• There is a constitutional requirement in India (Article 112) to present before the Parliament a statement of estimated receipts and expenditures of the government in respect of every financial year which runs from 1 April to 31 March.
 
• This ‘Annual Financial Statement’ constitutes the main budget document.
 
• Therefore, the budget comprises of the-Revenue Budget and the Capital Budget.
 
• The Revenue Budget shows the current receipts of the government and the expenditure that can be met from these receipts.
 
• Revenue receipts are receipts of the government which are non-redeemable, that is, they cannot be reclaimed from the government.
 
• They are divided into tax and non-tax revenues.
 
• They can not be claimed by the government under special circumstances.

questions.question: Mendeleev's Periodic Law was modified, and ___ was adopted as the basis of the Modern Periodic Table.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atomic number**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Henry Moseley observed that there is a relationship between wavelength and atomic number.
 
• Accordingly Mendeleev periodic law was modified and atomic number was adopted as the basis of modern periodic table.
 
• Atomic no. gives the number of proton in nucleus and the no. of electron in orbit around the nucleus.
 
• This number keeps on increasing by one when we move from one elements to others in a row.
 
• The properties of an elements could be predicted with more precision when they are arranged as per their increasing atomic no.
 
• Additionally the modern periodic table take cares of 3 limitation of Mendeleev periodic table.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Limitations of Mendeleev periodic table are as follows:**

 
 
• Electronic configuration of H resemble with that of alkali metals but it existed as a diatomic molecules just like halogen hence no fixed position could be given to H.
 
• Mendeleev could not assigned location to isotopes as they were discovered long after Mendeleev periodic table.
 
• Atomic masses do not increase in a regular manner, so it was not possible to predict how many elements could be discovered between 2 elements.

questions.question: On 8 April, 1929, Bhagat Singh and B.K. Dutt threw a bomb in the ____ The aim of the event as their leaflet explained, was not to kill but "to make the deaf hear".
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Central Legislative Assembly.**__

__
 
• On **8 April 1929**, Bhagat Singh and B.K. Dutt threw a bomb in the **Central Legislative Assembly** in Delhi.
 
• The act was intended to protest the Public Safety Bill passed by the British government in 1928.
 
• Their revolutionary group was the Hindustan Republican Socialist Association (HRSA), which sought to gain publicity for their cause.
 
• Objective: The aim was not to kill anyone but to make the British government “hear the voice of freedom fighters.”
 
• The leaflet they distributed after the bombing emphasized that the goal was not to kill anyone but "to make the deaf hear."
 
• The bombing was a peaceful act of defiance aimed at drawing attention to the oppressive legislation, not causing harm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Impact:** The event marked a significant moment in the Indian freedom struggle, highlighting the shift from non-violent to revolutionary tactics.
 
• Both Bhagat Singh and B.K. Dutt were arrested and later became national icons in the fight against British colonial rule.

questions.question: As of November 2023, how many Fundamental Duties are in the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**11**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Constitution of India** originally did not include **Fundamental Duties.**
 
• In **1976**, the **42nd Amendment Act added Fundamental Duties to the Constitutio**n, following the recommendations of the **Swaran Singh Committee.**
 
• Initially, **10 Fundamental Duties** were introduced.
 
• Later, an additional duty was added, making the total count **11 Fundamental Duties.**
 
• These duties are listed under **Article 51A in Part IV-A of the Constitution.**
 
• The aim of these duties is to promote national integrity, unity, and responsible citizenship.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The following is a list of 11 fundamental duties – **

 
 
• Abide by the Constitution and respect national flag & National Anthem
 
• Follow ideals of the freedom struggle
 
• Protect sovereignty & integrity of India
 
• Defend the country and render national services when called upon
 
• Developing the spirit of common brotherhood
 
• Preserve composite culture of the country
 
• Preserve natural environment
 
• Develop scientific temper and humanity
 
• Safeguard public property and avoid violence
 
• Strive for excellence in all spheres of life.
 
• Duty of all parents/guardians to send their children in the age group of 6-14 years to school.

questions.question: Which of the following festival is celebrated by Khamtis tribe of Arunachal Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Sangken.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sangken** is a water festival celebrated by the **Khamti tribe** of **Arunachal Pradesh.**
 
• It marks **the traditional New Year for the Khamti **and is also observed by other Tai ethnic groups in Northeast India.
 
• The festival involves the ceremonial bathing of Buddha statues and sprinkling water on each other as a sign of purification and goodwill.
 
• Sangken is celebrated around** mid-April**, coinciding with other Southeast Asian New Year festivals like Songkran in Thailand.
 
• The festival reflects **Buddhist cultural practices** and promotes harmony, peace, and community bonding.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khamti Tribe**: The Khamtis are one of the major Buddhist tribes in Arunachal Pradesh, belonging to the larger Tai ethnic group. They follow Theravada Buddhism.
 
• **Other Festivals**:
 
 
• **Tamladu**: A festival celebrated by the Digaru Mishmi tribe, it is a nature worship festival involving prayers for protection and prosperity.
 
• **Mopin**: Celebrated by the Galo tribe, Mopin is an agricultural festival to ensure a good harvest and is marked by dances, songs, and rituals.
 
• **Reh**: This is a festival of the Idu Mishmi tribe, held to honor the earth and ancestors, ensuring their protection and blessings.
 
 
 
• **Water Symbolism**: In Sangken, water symbolizes purification, renewal, and the washing away of past sins and negative emotions.
 
• **Buddhist Influence**: The rituals reflect Buddhist teachings, focusing on compassion, humility, and the cycle of life and rebirth.

questions.question: The Attorney-General for India shall hold office during the pleasure of the ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Attorney-General for India shall hold office during the pleasure of the **President**.
 
• **The term of office is not fixed** by the Constitution of India (COI).
 
• The Attorney-General may be **removed by the President at any time**.
 
• The **Attorney General of India** is appointed by the **President** of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The duties of the Attorney General of India include the following:**

 
 
• **Legal Advice**: To give advice to the Government of India on legal matters referred to him by the President.
 
• **Perform Legal Duties**: To perform other legal duties assigned by the President.
 
• **Discharge Functions**: To discharge functions conferred by the Constitution of India or any other law.
 
• **Supreme Court Representation**: To appear on behalf of the Government of India in all cases concerning it in the Supreme Court.
 
• **Represent the Government in References**: To represent the Government of India in any reference made by the President to the Supreme Court under Article 143 of the Constitution.
 
• **High Court Appearance:** To appear in any High Court case concerning the Government of India when required.

questions.question: Varahamihira's work Panchasiddhantika deals with ___ astronomical systems.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Five.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Varahamihira's work **Panchasiddhantika** discusses **five** astronomical systems.
 
• The term **Panchasiddhantika** translates to "The Five Astronomical Systems."
 
• This work synthesizes knowledge from earlier astronomical texts and systems.
 
• Varahamihira was a prominent Indian astronomer and mathematician of the 6th century CE.
 
• The five systems included are the **Surya Siddhanta, Romaka Siddhanta, Paulisha Siddhanta, Garga Siddhanta,** and **Vashishta Siddhanta**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Varahamihira**: An influential figure in ancient Indian astronomy, he was part of the 'Navaratnas' (Nine Gems) in the court of King Vikramaditya.
 
• **Panchasiddhantika**: This treatise compiled and commented on five key astronomical works, providing insights into their methodologies and findings.
 
• **Astronomical Systems**: Each system presents unique approaches to celestial calculations, including planetary motions, eclipses, and calendars.
 
• **Surya Siddhanta**: One of the most important texts, it forms the basis for many calculations in Indian astronomy and discusses the Earth's circumference and the solar system.
 
• **Significance of the Work**: **Panchasiddhantika** is significant for its contribution to the evolution of Indian astronomical knowledge and its influence on later scholars.

questions.question: ____, which belongs to Kerala in southern India, takes its name from the mythic enchantress Mohini.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohiniattam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mohiniyattam** is a classical dance form from Kerala, South India.
 
• The name **Mohiniyattam** comes from the mythic enchantress **Mohini**, who was the female form taken by Lord Vishnu.
 
• The dance form reflects the graceful and sensuous movements of **Mohini**, the enchantress from Hindu mythology.
 
• **Mohiniyattam** literally means "dance of the enchantress."

• **Key features of Mohiniyattam, the classical dance form of Kerala**, include:

 
 
• **Graceful Movements**: Characterized by slow, graceful, and sensuous movements, primarily performed by women, it reflects the enchanting nature of Mohini, the mythic figure.
 
• **Themes of Love and Devotion**: The dance revolves around themes of love and devotion, often dedicated to Lord Vishnu or his incarnation, Lord Krishna.
 
• **40 Adavukal (Basic Movements)**: Mohiniyattam comprises around 40 basic movements or adavukal, which are gentle and emphasize the swaying of the hips while maintaining a straight posture.
 
• **Mudras (Hand Gestures)**: The dance uses specific hand gestures (mudras), based on the ancient treatise Hastha Lakshanadeepika, to narrate stories through symbolic movements of fingers and palms.
 
• **Swaying Hips and Posture**: One of the defining aspects is the slow, rhythmic swaying of the hips with a straight posture that moves from side to side.
 
• **Costume**: The traditional attire consists of a white sari with a golden brocade (kasavu), symbolizing simplicity and elegance.
 
• **Musical Accompaniment**: The music is known as chollu, with lyrics in Manipravalam, a mix of Sanskrit and Malayalam.
 
• **Training Institutions**: Kerala Kalamandalam is one of the most prominent centers for learning Mohiniyattam.
